title: Learned serum-marker combinations improve internal melanoma progression classification
summary: In 323 early-stage melanoma patients, classifiers combined serum IL-4, GM-CSF and dermcidin with tumor thickness to distinguish subsequent metastatic progression. Nested internal validation supported added discrimination beyond thickness alone; this does not establish clinical benefit or external validity.
ai_technology: Regularized logistic regression; support vector machine; decision tree; naive Bayes; nearest neighbors
organization: University of the Basque Country; Biocruces Bizkaia Health Research Institute

evidence.tested: Classifiers were assessed with nested cross-validation in a clinical cohort with 74 metastatic outcomes. Scaling, oversampling, feature selection and tuning were assigned to the inner loop.
evidence.unknown: Internal validation only; unequal follow-up and incomplete sentinel-node information limit interpretation. This is postoperative risk classification, not diagnosis-time screening or an intervention benefit. Publisher first-online June 2 differs from the June 24 date in primary indexing metadata; the publisher date represents this journal version.
evidence.ai_role: Learned multivariable classifiers link measured circulating markers and tumor thickness to subsequent clinical outcomes.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher front date and safe clinical/statistical Methods and Results. Operational assay sections are outside the represented evidence.
